newsitem.title: GERMANY: Former Kohl secretary found guilty of espionage.
newsitem.headline: Former Kohl secretary found guilty of espionage.

text.p: A former secretary in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's office and her husband were found guilty by a state court on Friday of spying for East Germany during the 1980s.
The court sentenced the couple to two years probation and a 25,000 mark ($18,000) fine.

The 44-year-old woman, named by justice officials only as Karin H.-P., had admitted she and her husband had friendly contact with East Germany's notorious Stasi security police, but denied she had passed on any confidential documents.

Judge Guenter Krantz said there was no concrete damage done to West Germany because of the defendant's Stasi contacts, but he said there was a potential for severe danger to the state. The defendant, for example, never made any requests for sensitive documents.
The woman admitted she and her husband had friendly contact with Stasi workers but said she had not passed on any confidential documents.

Prosecutors said the woman, who worked in the chancellery from 1981 to 1989 first under Helmut Schmidt and then under Kohl, had spied for the Stasi under the codename "Britta". They said she had made contact with the Stasi on about 20 occasions between 1981 and 1993.
